trust_decision.summary: Whether a caller's option object is trusted to supply values: only own enumerable properties may be used, copied onto a prototype-less object, at the ThreadPool defaults merge, the Piscina constructor (including the EventEmitterAsyncResource super call), run() and close(). Anything reachable through the options prototype chain must be ignored.

landing_point.why: The summary points at ThreadPool.options, i.e. this exact merge `{ ...kDefaultOptions, ...options, filename, maxQueue: 0 }`: the spread drops inherited properties but the result is an ordinary object, so the keys read later at src/index.ts:209 (loadBalancer) and src/index.ts:237-242 (env, argv, execArgv, resourceLimits, workerData) resolve through Object.prototype.

fix_sites.entry_point: shared helper used by the constructor, run() and close() (new export from src/common.ts)
new Piscina(options) -> ThreadPool constructor defaults merge
fix_sites.module_kind: core class constructor / defaults merge route

fix_sites.entry_point: new Piscina(options), including the options object handed to EventEmitterAsyncResource via super()
new Piscina(options) option validation (resourceLimits read from the raw user object; changed in fix commits 5be7bbb and bebbda2 only)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about worker exec options (execArgv / env / loadBalancer), and the object passed to EventEmitterAsyncResource carries a fixed internal name 'Piscina', so an inherited triggerAsyncId/requireManualDestroy looks like Node's async_hooks business rather than part of the pool's option handling.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate own values of env, argv, execArgv and workerData must still be forwarded to the worker exactly as given, and pool.options must remain a fully-defaulted, readable copy (maxQueue 'auto' resolving to maxThreads**2). An over-broad fix that allow-lists, strips, freezes or deep-clones option values breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: global Object.prototype pollution (the three tests the fix adds: execArgv / loadBalancer / env)
per-object prototype set by an object literal '{"__proto__": polluted}' in the options argument (already tested at the pinned commit for filename/name)
Object.setPrototypeOf(options, polluted) on an existing options object
options created with Object.create(proto) so option names are inherited rather than own
own '__proto__' data property on an options object (e.g. from JSON.parse), which must stay a plain key
omitted options argument, falling back to kDefaultOptions / kDefaultRunOptions / kDefaultCloseOptions

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Worker options are rebuilt as a fresh plain object immediately before the real sink: `const { filename, ...workerOpts } = worker; new Worker(filename, workerOpts)` re-materialises Object.prototype under the options Node reads, so keys piscina does not explicitly forward are still inherited.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The report's gadget is piscina's own option copy; this object is a local reconstruction handed to Node, so whatever Node reads beyond the keys piscina forwards is Node's option contract, not piscina's option handling.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another module directory (src/worker_pool), one import hop from src/index.ts, and the published fix never touched it

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Constructor validation reads resourceLimits from the raw user object (`options.resourceLimits`) while every neighbouring validation reads the null-prototype copy `opts`, so an inherited resourceLimits reaches a check the fix's other sites no longer reach.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is only a validation read: a polluted resourceLimits can at most make the constructor throw, it cannot install a worker option, so it does not belong to the execArgv/env/loadBalancer gadget.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~40 lines above the run() site, but a different read path (raw options, not the sanitised copy)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second per-task defaults merge in ThreadPool.runTask (`{ ...kDefaultRunOptions, ...options }`) whose keys are resolved the same way.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: run(options) already mirrors pool options (filename, name, signal, transferList), so adding one more per-task field resolved through the options object is the obvious next change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another Worker option (stdout/stderr/stdin/name) added by spreading pool options into workerOpts at the Worker construction site.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: That destructure-and-spread literal is the natural place a maintainer adds a worker flag, and it is one module away from where every existing worker option is read.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second derived-option route (like maxQueue 'auto' -> maxThreads**2, or loadBalancer selection) that reads this.options after the merge.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The constructor already post-processes the merged object in place, so new derived options keep being added next to the sink rather than to the defaults table.

O9_family: Prototype pollution of an options object leading to worker option injection / RCE (CWE-1321 improper control of object prototype attributes)

O10_build.toolchain: Node >= 22 (package.json engines), tsc via typescript ^6 with gen-esm-wrapper for the ESM facade; tests run on node:test through scripts/run-tests.js with --import=tsx; jest config also present

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Harden run() the way the existing filename/name tests already do (hasOwnProperty / delete the polluted keys on the user's options object) and leave this.options at src/index.ts:188 as an ordinary spread, so execArgv/env/loadBalancer are still inherited at src/index.ts:209 and 237-242.

out_of_scope_notes: src/task_queue/index.ts:138-140 resolves queue options from the user's task object through the exported queueOptionsSymbol; a polluted Object.prototype carrying that symbol would reach custom TaskQueue implementations - a different sink from the pool's worker options, not pursued.

src/index.ts:1005-1017 (Piscina.move / isTransferable) inspects symbol-keyed properties on user values; symbol-keyed pollution is a different vector and is not part of this advisory's protection, not pursued.
